regimens.indication: Treatment of Tonic-Clonic (Grand Mal) and Psychomotor (Temporal Lobe) Seizures

refs.quote: DILANTIN is indicated for the treatment of tonic-clonic (grand mal) and psychomotor (temporal lobe) seizures and prevention and treatment of seizures occurring during or following neurosurgery. ( 1 )

The recommended starting dose for adult patients who have received no previous treatment is one 100-mg DILANTIN (extended phenytoin sodium capsule, USP) by mouth three times daily. Adjust the dosage to suit individual requirements up to a maximum of two capsules three times a day. For most adults, the satisfactory maintenance dosage will be one capsule three to four times a day.

regimens.dose_text: Adult starting dose in previously untreated patients is 100 mg orally three times daily. Satisfactory maintenance dose for most adults is 300 to 400 mg daily (divided 100 mg 3 to 4 times daily, or 300 mg once daily once seizure control is established). Titrate based on serum concentration determinations (target 10 to 20 mcg/mL).

hepatic.value: The liver is the chief site of biotransformation of phenytoin; patients with impaired liver function may show early signs of toxicity. Because the fraction of unbound phenytoin is increased in hepatic disease or hypoalbuminemia, monitor unbound phenytoin concentrations.

refs.quote: The liver is the chief site of biotransformation of phenytoin; patients with impaired liver function, elderly patients, or those who are gravely ill may show early signs of toxicity.

The precise mechanism by which phenytoin exerts its therapeutic effect has not been established but is thought to involve the voltage-dependent blockade of membrane sodium channels resulting in a reduction in sustained high-frequency neuronal discharges.

mg_safety.note: Phenytoin may impair neuromuscular transmission and exacerbate muscle weakness in myasthenia gravis; use with extreme caution

value.instructions: Prompt-release chewable tablets may be crushed; extended-release capsules should not be crushed. Enteral feeding formulas bind phenytoin and decrease bioavailability: hold continuous tube feedings 1 to 2 hours before and after administration and monitor serum levels closely.

refs.locator: Section ADVERSE REACTIONS - Skin and Appendages
refs.quote: Dermatological manifestations sometimes accompanied by fever have included scarlatiniform or morbilliform rashes. A morbilliform rash (measles-like) is the most common; other types of dermatitis are seen more rarely.

value.effect: Inhibition of CYP2C9 and CYP2C19 saturable metabolism produces rapid, non-linear surges in serum phenytoin levels leading to cerebellar toxicity.
value.management: Monitor phenytoin concentrations closely and anticipate dose reductions when initiating these agents.

refs.quote: Inhibition of metabolism may produce significant increases in circulating phenytoin concentrations and enhance the risk of drug toxicity.

value.effect: Potent hepatic microsomal enzyme induction by phenytoin accelerates steroid clearance, risking unplanned pregnancy or loss of corticosteroid efficacy.
value.management: Recommend alternative non-hormonal contraception or increase corticosteroid doses as clinically required.
